title: Optimize a slow query
objectives: Find where a query spends its time
Rewrite filters so the engine can skip work
Prove a faster query still gives the same answer

exercises.prompt: This query returns each store's revenue from completed 2026 orders, but slowly. Make it at least twice as fast without changing its answer.
hints: Look at the WHERE clause. What does the engine have to do to every one of the two million rows before it can compare them?

CAST(order_date AS VARCHAR) turns two million dates into text before any of them is compared. A date range compares order_date as it is, which is cheaper, and on a table sorted by date it lets the engine skip whole blocks of rows.
The IN subquery reads the whole orders table again to find one status. Which status counts as a sale?
